USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

New symptoms during treatment

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient treating presumed seasonal eye allergy with ketotifen develops unilateral eye pain and reduced vision the next morning. Itching had been the initial symptom, but the new symptoms are different. What is the most appropriate next step?

  1. Increase dosing frequency until vision improves
  2. Assume reduced vision confirms the intended drug effect
  3. Cover the symptoms with contact lenses
  4. Continue unchanged for several weeks before seeking care
  5. Stop self-treatment and obtain prompt eye assessment
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Stop self-treatment and obtain prompt eye assessment

Pain and visual change are warning symptoms; they should not be assumed to be uncomplicated allergy.

Understanding the options

Stop self-treatment and obtain prompt eye assessment
Pain and visual change are warning symptoms; they should not be assumed to be uncomplicated allergy.
Increase dosing frequency until vision improves
Exceeding labeled use delays evaluation of potentially serious disease.
Assume reduced vision confirms the intended drug effect
Visual loss is not a desired therapeutic effect.
Cover the symptoms with contact lenses
Lenses do not address the cause and may worsen some ocular problems.
Continue unchanged for several weeks before seeking care
New pain and visual change warrant timely assessment.
